raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-cu134` (and every dated `nightly-cu134-*` tag) is published for **arm64 only**: `release-docker-cu134-nightly.yml` builds only on `arm-kernel-build-node` with `--platform linux/arm64`. x86_64 Blackwell and Hopper hosts (B300, B200, H200) have no CUDA 13.4 nightly to pull (`docker pull` fails with `no matching manifest for linux/amd64`). Models whose kernels need a CUDA 13.4 toolkit at runtime, such as MiniMax-M3.1-Flash (the MSA `qmul4` NVFP4 KV dequant compiles with `nvcc` >= 13.4), are left on one-off `dev-*` images on x86.

`docker/Dockerfile.cu134` already handles x86_64 (CUDA target by `uname -m`, sm90-only HPC-Ops and the flash-attn3 cubin download on x86). Only the `MANYLINUX_IMAGE` default is aarch64-specific.

## Modifications

`.github/workflows/release-docker-cu134-nightly.yml`:

- **`meta` job.** Computes the date / commit tag once, so both architectures and the merged tags share it.
- **`build` matrix.** `amd64` on `x64-kernel-build-node` (the runner the kernel and DeepEP wheel releases use for x86_64) with `MANYLINUX_IMAGE=pytorch/manylinux2_28-builder:cuda13.4`, and `arm64` on `arm-kernel-build-node` as before. `fail-fast: false`, so one architecture failing does not cancel the other's multi-hour build. `--builder default` is kept, so each node's BuildKit / ccache stays warm. Each architecture pushes to a rolling single-arch tag (`nightly-cu134-amd64` / `nightly-cu134-arm64`) and uploads the pushed repo digest as an artifact.
- **`merge` job.** `docker buildx imagetools create` writes `nightly-cu134-{date}-{sha}` and `nightly-cu134` from the digests. arm64 is required (current GB200 / GB300 users must not lose it); amd64 is added when it built, otherwise the run publishes arm64 only with a `::warning::`. If arm64 failed, nothing is published and the job fails.
- `build_only` dispatches still build both architectures and skip the push and merge, as before.

The single-arch rolling tags do not match the nightly cleanup pattern `^nightly-cu134-[0-9]`, so only two extra tags ever exist.

## Testing

- `actionlint` is clean apart from the warnings the existing workflow already has (custom self-hosted runner labels, `docker/login-action@v2`).
- **Not run yet:** the x86_64 build itself. Suggested check before merge: dispatch this workflow on this branch with `build_only=true`, or with `image_repo=lmsysorg/sglang-staging`. Then confirm `docker buildx imagetools inspect lmsysorg/sglang-staging:nightly-cu134` lists both `linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests (n/a: workflow-only change).
- [ ] Update documentation (n/a).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results (n/a).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

files.patch:
@@ -1,9 +1,11 @@
 name: Release Docker Images Nightly (CUDA 13.4 Rubin)
 #
 # Builds and publishes nightly CUDA 13.4 / Rubin (sm_107) images from
-# docker/Dockerfile.cu134, aarch64 only:
+# docker/Dockerfile.cu134 for x86_64 and aarch64, merged into multi-arch tags:
 #   - lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-cu134-{date}-{sha}
 #   - lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-cu134
+# Each architecture is also pushed to a rolling single-arch tag
+# (nightly-cu134-amd64 / nightly-cu134-arm64) that the merge step reads by digest.
 #
 
 on:
@@ -31,21 +33,15 @@ concurrency:
   cancel-in-progress: true
 
 jobs:
-  build-arm64:
+  # Computed once so both architectures and the merged tags share one date and commit.
+  meta:
     if: github.repository == 'sgl-project/sglang'
-    # Use kernel builder node since we need to build wheels from source.
-    runs-on: arm-kernel-build-node
-    environment: ${{ (github.event_name == 'schedule' || !inputs.build_only) && 'prod' || null }}
-    # Cold builds recompile three CUDA wheels from source.
-    timeout-minutes: 360
-
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    outputs:
+      image_repo: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.image_repo }}
+      tag: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}
+      tag_rolling: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag_rolling }}
     steps:
-      - name: Delete huge unnecessary tools folder
-        run: rm -rf /opt/hostedtoolcache
-
-      - name: Cleanup workspace (remove root-owned files from prior runs)
-        run: sudo rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/* || true
-
       - name: Checkout repository
         uses: actions/checkout@v4
 
@@ -60,6 +56,37 @@ jobs:
           echo "tag=nightly-cu134-${date_tag}-${commit_hash}"              >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
           echo "tag_rolling=nightly-cu134"                                 >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
 
+  build:
+    needs: meta
+    strategy:
+      # One architecture failing must not cancel the other's multi-hour build.
+      fail-fast: false
+      matrix:
+        include:
+          - arch: amd64
+            # Use kernel builder nodes since we need to build wheels from source.
+            runner: x64-kernel-build-node
+            manylinux_image: pytorch/manylinux2_28-builder:cuda13.4
+          - arch: arm64
+            runner: arm-kernel-build-node
+            manylinux_image: pytorch/manylinuxaarch64-builder:cuda13.4
+    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
+    environment: ${{ (github.event_name == 'schedule' || !inputs.build_only) && 'prod' || null }}
+    # Cold builds recompile three CUDA wheels from source.
+    timeout-minutes: 360
+    env:
+      IMAGE_ARCH_REF: ${{ needs.meta.outputs.image_repo }}:${{ needs.meta.outputs.tag_rolling }}-${{ matrix.arch }}
+
+    steps:
+      - name: Delete huge unnecessary tools folder
+        run: rm -rf /opt/hostedtoolcache
+
+      - name: Cleanup workspace (remove root-owned files from prior runs)
+        run: sudo rm -rf "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"/* || true
+
+      - name: Checkout repository
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+
       - name: Login to Docker Hub
         if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || !inputs.build_only
         uses: docker/login-action@v2
@@ -73,14 +100,14 @@ jobs:
           docker buildx build \
             --builder default \
             --progress=plain \
-            --platform linux/arm64 \
+            --platform "linux/${{ matrix.arch }}" \
             --target "${{ inputs.docker_target || 'runtime' }}" \
             --build-arg BRANCH_TYPE=local \
             --build-arg BUILD_TYPE=all \
             --build-arg BUILD_JOBS="$(nproc)" \
+            --build-arg MANYLINUX_IMAGE="${{ matrix.manylinux_image }}" \
             -f docker/Dockerfile.cu134 \
-            -t "${{ steps.meta.outputs.image_repo }}:${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}" \
-            -t "${{ steps.meta.outputs.image_repo }}:${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag_rolling }}" \
+            -t "${IMAGE_ARCH_REF}" \
             .
 
       - name: Push image
@@ -95,11 +122,74 @@ jobs:
             done
             return 1
           }
-          push_with_retry "${{ steps.meta.outputs.image_repo }}:${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}"
-          push_with_retry "${{ steps.meta.outputs.image_repo }}:${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag_rolling }}"
+          push_with_retry "${IMAGE_ARCH_REF}"
+          # The repo digest of what was just pushed, so the merge step does not depend
+          # on the rolling tag still pointing at this build.
+          digest_ref="$(docker inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' "${IMAGE_ARCH_REF}")"
+          echo "Pushed ${digest_ref}"
+          mkdir -p digests
+          echo "${digest_ref}" > "digests/${{ matrix.arch }}.txt"
+
+      - name: Upload image digest
+        if: github.event_name == 'schedule' || !inputs.build_only
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          name: cu134-digest-${{ matrix.arch }}
+          path: digests/${{ matrix.arch }}.txt
+          retention-days: 1
 
       - name: Cleanup local images
         if: always()
+        run: docker rmi -f "${IMAGE_ARCH_REF}" || true
+
+  merge:
+    needs: [meta, build]
+    # Runs after a partial failure too; the step below decides what to publish.
+    if: always() && needs.meta.result == 'success' && (github.event_name == 'schedule' || !inputs.build_only)
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    environment: prod
+    steps:
+      - name: Download image digests
+        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
+        with:
+          pattern: cu134-digest-*
+          path: digests
+          merge-multiple: true
+
+      - name: Set up Docker Buildx
+        uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3
+
+      - name: Login to Docker Hub
+        uses: docker/login-action@v2
+        with:
+          username: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_USERNAME }}
+          password: ${{ secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN }}
+
+      - name: Create multi-arch tags
+        env:
+          IMAGE_REPO: ${{ needs.meta.outputs.image_repo }}
+          TAG: ${{ needs.meta.outputs.tag }}
+          TAG_ROLLING: ${{ needs.meta.outputs.tag_rolling }}
         run: |
-          docker rmi -f "${{ steps.meta.outputs.image_repo }}:${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag }}" || true
-          docker rmi -f "${{ steps.meta.outputs.image_repo }}:${{ steps.meta.outputs.tag_rolling }}" || true
+          set -euo pipefail
+          ls -la digests || true
+          # digests/<arch>.txt holds "<repo>@sha256:..." for each architecture that
+          # built and pushed. arm64 is required: GB200 / GB300 users already pull
+          # these tags, and the aarch64 image must not be dropped from them.
+          # amd64 joins when it built; a missing amd64 publishes arm64 only, with a warning.
+          if [ ! -f digests/arm64.txt ]; then
+            echo "::error::arm64 build did not push; not updating ${TAG} / ${TAG_ROLLING}"
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          SOURCES=("$(cat digests/arm64.txt)")
+          if [ -f digests/amd64.txt ]; then
+            SOURCES+=("$(cat digests/amd64.txt)")
+          else
+            echo "::warning::amd64 build did not push; ${TAG} is arm64 only"
+          fi
+
+          docker buildx imagetools create \
+            -t "${IMAGE_REPO}:${TAG}" \
+            -t "${IMAGE_REPO}:${TAG_ROLLING}" \
+            "${SOURCES[@]}"
+          docker buildx imagetools inspect "${IMAGE_REPO}:${TAG}"
